title: The remaining popups: file details and tags

steps.path: Marketplace → a plugin → open a skill or command file
steps.headline: Should file popups keep their two-line header when we compare the new divider and fade?
steps.today: The file viewer shows a small line naming the plugin and file type above a larger file name. A full-width line separates it from the scrolling file; the content does not fade at the edges.
steps.problem: Replacing the whole header with a compact single title could make it less clear which plugin a file belongs to. Keeping the larger title may also make this popup look different from Settings and Project details.
steps.proposal: Choose which header structure to carry into a visual Before/After comparison. The divider and fade themselves will be shown separately before any change is applied.

options.label: Keep both lines
pros: You can see the plugin and file name together.
The existing file context stays familiar.
cons: The header stays taller than a standard dialog.

options.label: One compact title
pros: Matches the smaller Project and dialog headers more closely.
cons: The plugin and file type move into the body or disappear from the header.

options.label: Leave this popup alone
pros: The file viewer keeps its current hierarchy and edge.
cons: Its full-width line and abrupt scrolling edge remain different from the approved popups.

steps.headline: Should the small Tags & note popup get the same edge treatment?
steps.today: This narrow editor has a 14px bold title and a full-width divider. Its body can scroll when the window is short or the tag list grows, but normally it fits without scrolling. Manage Tags opens a separate shared dialog that already has the approved treatment.
steps.problem: A permanent fade could dim tag controls in a short editor, while leaving the long state with a hard edge may feel inconsistent.
steps.proposal: Choose what to compare visually. Any fade would appear only while content is hidden above or below, not on a body that fits.

options.label: Line and scroll fade
pros: Matches the approved popups when tags overflow.
cons: Items near a scrolling edge briefly become faint.

options.label: Line only
pros: Makes the header consistent without fading controls.

options.label: Leave it as is
pros: Keeps this unusually small editor familiar.
cons: Its full-width divider remains different from Settings and other dialogs.
